page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 48 physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz. The system allocates 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable. The processor features a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, VAES cryptography, and AMD SVM virtualization.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ams_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and Geekbench multi-core scores. Its memory subsystem delivers strong read-only bandwidth, reaching 7,120.47 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 226.16 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded decompression is highly efficient, with bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier speeds of 626.48 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance achieves 112.7 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and strong Passmark database operation scores. Large language model inference speeds are strong for small to medium models, though performance drops to average levels when processing larger 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU acceleration.

The F48ams_v6 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity alongside dedicated, high-frequency CPU resources. Because it provides a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with dedicated physical cores, it avoids the resource contention typical of shared-core environments. However, the lack of bundled local storage means storage costs must be factored in separately via premium storage attachments. This server type is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, image processing, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
